name: Nṛhari Tīrtha
add: Nandgram Dham: born Svāmī Śāstrī (also Śāma or Śyāma Śāstrī). B. N. K. Sharma: born c. 1241, active in Kaliṅga 1264–1294, disappeared 1333; Śrīla Prabhupāda's list gives Śaka 1127 (c. 1205) for his birth; the gap is unresolved. Minister and then regent of the Eastern Gaṅga kingdom of Kaliṅga, as his own inscriptions at Śrīkūrmam and Simhācalam confirm. Works: Bhāva-prakāśikā (on Madhva's Gītā-bhāṣya) and commentaries on several of the ten Prakaraṇas; tradition credits him with fifteen works, of which only fragments survive.

name: Nārāyaṇa Bhaṭṭa
add: Nandgram Dham: held in his tradition to be an avatāra of Nārada Muni (Vraja-bhakti-vilāsa, Hindi edition). He came to Vraja c. 1545–46 and wrote the Vraja-bhakti-vilāsa at Rādhā-kuṇḍa c. 1552–53; known as Vrajācārya, informally «the seventh Gosvāmī». His disappearance is not reliably recorded.

name: Nārāyaṇa Paṇḍit
add: Nandgram Dham: the fourteenth branch of the Caitanya tree (Ādi 10.36, citing Caitanya-bhāgavata Antya 8.36); associated with Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura's household in Navadvīpa; he went to Purī with Rāma Paṇḍita, Śrīvāsa's brother. Often confused with the author of the Prema-vilāsa, who was Nityānanda dāsa. His birth and death are not recorded.

name: Śrī Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura
add: Nandgram Dham: the Narottama-vilāsa places his birth in 1534 and his disappearance in 1611; most sources do not fix the years. Campaka-mañjarī assists Rūpa-mañjarī in her service. Major works: Prārthanā and Prema-bhakti-candrikā.

name: Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu
add: Nandgram Dham: Balarāma, the second member of the Pañca-tattva (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 11; Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 1.28); sent by Śrī Caitanya to work in Bengal; known as Patita-pāvana, the deliverer of the fallen.

name: Śrī Padmanābha Tīrtha
add: Nandgram Dham: before sannyāsa, Śobhana Bhaṭṭa. He became Madhva's disciple c. 1265 on the Godāvarī, probably near Puntamba or Paithan; traditionally the first to head the pīṭha after Madhva, the first pontiff counted by the Uttarādi Maṭha. About fifteen works, including the Sattarka-dīpāvalī, Nyāya-ratnāvalī and Sannyāya-ratnāvalī, and commentaries on the Gītā-bhāṣya and the ten Prakaraṇas.

name: Paramānanda Purī
add: Nandgram Dham: his sannyāsī godbrothers include Īśvara Purī, Rāmacandra Purī, Brahmānanda Bhāratī and Keśava Bhāratī. In Purī he had a room in Kāśī Miśra's house, and his own small maṭha and well near the Jagannātha temple. His disappearance is not recorded.

name: Parameśvara Dāsa Ṭhākura
add: Nandgram Dham: the fifth of the twelve gopālas (Ādi 11.29 and Anubhāṣya); his descendants carry the titles Adhikārī and Gupta. His disappearance festival is kept on the Vaiśākha full moon at the Āṭapura temple.

name: Parameśvara Modaka
add: Nandgram Dham: «modaka», confectioner, records the family trade. His wife is named in the text only as «Mukundāra Mātā»; the Lord told him: «Parameśvara, may you be blessed. It is very good that you have come here» (Antya 12.54–60).

name: Śrīpad Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī
add: Nandgram Dham: younger brother of Tirumalaya Bhaṭṭa and elder brother of Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa, of a Śrī Vaiṣṇava priestly family of the Rāmānuja line; turned by the Lord during His four-month stay at Śrīraṅgam (1433 Śaka, 1511). He lived later at Kāmyavana, then in Vṛndāvana. Works: Śrī Rādhā-rasa-sudhā-nidhi, Śrī Caitanya-candrāmṛta, Śrī Vṛndāvana-mahimāmṛta, Navadvīpa-śataka.

name: Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī (Bhāratī)
add: Nandgram Dham: the thirteenth branch of the Caitanya tree (Ādi 10.35); Lord Nṛsiṁha was manifest in his heart, and the Lord appeared to him by āvirbhāva (Antya 2.5–6). He fed the Lord in meditation at Kumārahaṭṭa. His birth and death are not recorded.

name: Pradyumna Miśra
add: Nandgram Dham: his home is Śrīhaṭṭa by one tradition, Orissa by another. He was called «Dāsa», a mark of respect among Oḍiyā brāhmaṇas, not the low-caste title the word carries in Bengal; the sixth in the list of associates the Lord was overjoyed to meet (Ādi 10.131).

name: Gajapati Pratāparudra Deva
add: Nandgram Dham: of the Sūryavaṁśa Gajapati dynasty; reigned c. 1497–1540, capital Cuttack (later Khurda); chief queen Gaurī Devī. Refused an audience by the Lord for years, he was embraced after sweeping the Ratha-yātrā road and approaching Him in disguise.

name: Śrī Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi
add: Nandgram Dham: his associates also called him Ācāryanidhi.

name: Purandara Ācārya
add: Nandgram Dham: the ninth branch of the Caitanya tree; known also from Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 11.159–160. His guru, birth and death are not recorded.

name: Puruṣottama Dāsa
add: Nandgram Dham: of a vaidya family of Nāgaradeśa, a cluster of villages in Bengal; probably born early in the 16th century. Nandgram Dham identifies him as Dāma, the tenth of the twelve gopālas (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 131), where the record has Stoka-kṛṣṇa (130). His disappearance is not recorded in its sources.
